 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TUSHAR RAO GEDELA  ORDER % 14.03.2023 [ The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode ]

1. This is an application under Order VI Rule 17 read with Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 (in short "CPC") filed on behalf of the appellant seeking certain amendments to the original appeal as filed before this Court.

entities.text: Order VI Rule 17 read with Section 151
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 2. There is no opposition on behalf of the respondents.
3. The application is allowed.
4. The amended appeal may be taken on record and numbered accordingly.
5. The application stands disposed of.
6. This is an application on behalf of the appellant under Section 149 read with Section 151 CPC seeking extension of time to file Court fees.

sentences.text: It has been submitted by learned ASG that the Court fees on the amount which is specified in the amended appeal has already been affixed.
8. In view of the above, the application stands disposed of.
CM APPL. 10071/2023 (Stay) CM APPL. 10072/2023 (Delay in filing) CM APPL. 10073/2023 (Delay in re-filing)

9. The appellant challenges the impugned judgment and decree dated 19.07.2022 passed by the Reference Court in LAC 3/2018 titled 'Renu Saini & Ors. vs. UOI', whereby the compensation amount as awarded by the LAC was enhanced from Rs.53 Lakhs per acre i.e., Rs. 1095/- per sq. yd.
to Rs.65,860/- per sq. yd. in respect of the land of the respondents/petitioners which was acquired.
Other statutory entitlements were also calculated thereon, on the said principal amount.
10. The subject land was acquired by the LAC for the user department, which is respondent no.2/Delhi Jal Board forming part of Village Jasola, Delhi for the purposes of planned development of Delhi.

11. Mr. Sanjay Jain, learned ASG appearing for the appellant submits that the learned Reference Court has primarily based its judgment and decree on the basis of the judgment rendered in 'Nirmala Devi Aggarwal & Anr. vs. UOI & Anr.' LAC No. 09/2015, and submits that the said basis itself is erroneous and the application of the ratio in that particular case is not at all applicable in the present appeal.

entities.text: Nirmala Devi Aggarwal & Anr. vs. UOI & Anr.' LAC No. 09/2015
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Learned ASG submits that in the present case, the user department is a public utility and the purpose for which the land has been acquired and handed over to Delhi Jal Board, the user department, should be the basis of deciding what the awarded amount or even the enhanced amount ought to be.

Learned ASG submits that the judgment in the case of Nirmala Devi (supra) is pending adjudication before this Court and is listed on 20.07.2023, however, the present matter may not be listed alongwith that matter for consideration for the aforesaid reason.

13. This Court is today considering only the stay application preferred by the user department i.e.,
Delhi Jal Board and the principles of Order XLI Rule 5 of CPC has to be applied inasmuch as the impugned order and decree is revenue/money decree.
14. Mr. Jain, learned ASG submits that the appellant is a public utility service, supplying water to the city of Delhi and does not derive any financial benefit out of the usage of the said land.
Learned ASG also submits that a Sewage Treatment Plant is being run and maintained by the Jal Board on the said land and it is apparent that no financial benefits accrue from such use.

On that basis,
learned ASG submits that it would be onerous and burdensome upon the appellant Jal Board to be expected to deposit any amount at all, in lieu of the orders to be obtained on the stay application.

15. Learned ASG also submits that since water is an essential service, the Jal Board is under a Constitutional obligation to ensure that clean drinking water is supplied to all sections of society Delhi Jal Board vs Renu Saini & Ors on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90074150/
2

entities.text: Delhi Jal Board vs Renu Saini & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: including the deprived sections and the sewage which is generated has also to be managed.
On that basis, learned ASG submits that it is an absolutely non-commercial utility and expecting the appellant to make any pre-deposit cannot be countenanced.

16. Per Contra, Mr. Gaurav Sarin, learned counsel appearing for respondents 1 to 8 draws attention of this Court to page 30 of the appeal paper book, which is the impugned judgment, particularly to para 13 to submit that no evidence at all was led on behalf of respondent no.2 therein, which is the Delhi Jal Board and the right to lead evidence was closed.

On that basis, Mr. Sarin submits that despite having been given a chance, the Jal Board did not explain its situation before the Reference Court and it is too late in the day to put across the submissions as made by learned ASG.

17 . Mr. Sarin also draws attention of this Court to page 41, particularly para-18 of the impugned order, to submit that the statutory dues which have been calculated upon the enhanced amount are not amounts which are detachable from the enhanced amount for the reasons that the same are dues which are statutory in nature and are provided as a matter of right to the persons who are deprived of the land and that too, under Land Acquisition Act, whereby the acquisition is in the nature of compulsory acquisition of land.
Learned counsel submits that the respondents have been deprived of such lands permanently.
18. Mr. Sarin, learned counsel also submits that having regard to the fact that though, deprivation took place in the year 1989, till date, the respondents have not received the enhanced amounts.
Learned counsel also submits that the submission that the Appellant is a public utility and does not generate any revenue is concerned, the same is without any basis.

Learned counsel submits that the Jal Board has a monopoly in supply of water to the entire city of Delhi and revenue is generated in hundreds of crores of rupees every year and thus submits that it is not a case where the appellant is without generating revenue at all.
Mr. Sarin submits that it may be so, that in the present land sewage treatment plant is being run, however, the department as a whole does not suffer from lack of generation of revenue.

19. Mr. Sarin also submits that the land which has been acquired has a very high commercial potentiality, in that, the land is stated to be situated in between New Friends Colony and Apollo Hospital and is abutting the National Highway connecting Delhi to Mathura and therefore, the usage for which the Jal Board may now put the land to, is of no consequence, so far as the respondents are concerned.
20. On that basis, Mr. Sarin submits that this Court should direct 100% deposit of the decretal amount.
21. This Court has considered the rival submissions of learned ASG on one hand and Mr. Sarin on the other.

22. It has been informed that the land in question was acquired by the LAC/UOI for the user department i.e. the appellant/Delhi Jal Board and it is in process of filing an appeal against the very same impugned order before this Court.

It has been given to understand that as on the date of the Delhi Jal Board vs Renu Saini & Ors on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90074150/
3 decree would be around Rs. 151 Crores.

entities.text: Delhi Jal Board vs Renu Saini & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the said amount is disputed by the appellant herein.

23. The appellant had also filed an application seeking amendment of the present appeal and has valued the appeal for the purposes of Court fee at Rs.150 Crores and ad valorem Court fee has also been affixed thereon.

24. No doubt that the appellant is a public utility and may be operating sewage treatment plant in the acquired land, however, that itself would not be indicative of the revenue that is being generated by the Delhi Jal Board in the ordinary course of its conduct of business.
It is also correct that the revenue which is generated is not in terms of the commercial enhancement but only run as a non-profit making organisation.

25. Learned ASG has brought to this Court's notice the provisions of Section 55 of the Delhi Jal Board which reads as under:-
"Charge for services rendered.

55. (1) The board shall for the purpose of the services rendered by it under the act levy fees, charges, including development charges, rentals and collect deposits and may recover interest on amount payable to it, at such rates as may be specified by regulations.

(2) The fees, charges, rentals and deposits referred to in sub - section (1) shall be so fixed as overall to ensure the recovery of all costs of operation, maintenance,
repayment of debt and a return of not less than three percent on next fixed assets.
Provided that development charges in respect of any building or part thereof or of any group of cluster of buildings shall not be less than the actual expenditure incurred."
26. Keeping in view the aforesaid provision, prima facie, it appears that the appellant does not generate any revenue of commercial nature.

27. Be that as it may, since there is an award in terms of impugned judgment and decree, enhancing the rate at which the LAC has granted per square yard of the acquired land, it would be in the interest of justice to direct Delhi Jal Board, the appellant herein to deposit a sum of Rs.50 Crores in this Court in the name of Registrar General of this Court.
28. The said amount be deposited in three instalments.
The first instalment of Rs.20 Crores be deposited within 30 days from today.
The next instalment of Rs.15 Crores be deposited within 30 days thereafter and the third instalment of Rs.15 Crores be deposited in next 30 days thereafter.
The said amount shall be invested in an interest bearing FDR with auto- renewal facility by the Registrar General.

Upon such deposit, the impugned order shall remain stayed till further orders.
30. It is made clear that the interest component on the entire decretal mount shall only be inoperative to the extent of amount which has been deposited before this Court.
31. In view of the aforesaid order, the Executing Court shall defer its proceedings stated to be listed on 15.03.2023 to a date beyond the date fixed by this Court.
32. Reply may be filed within six weeks.

Rejoinder thereto if any, may be filed within six weeks,
thereafter.
